$comment: Known-failing test files, by path. Maintained by tools/test-ratchet.mjs.
A failure NOT listed here is a regression and blocks. A file listed here that now
passes ALSO blocks, with 'lower the baseline' -- a ratchet that silently absorbs
improvement stops ratcheting.
SEEDED from a COMPLETE full-tree run: 2026-08-11T16:27:26.210Z, 76/76 batches, 737 files
requested and 737 recorded, 699 pass / 35 fail / 1 timeout / 2 skip, 36.1 minutes
wall clock, 0 not-run and 0 no-record. Command:
node tools/test-run.js --all --output <scratch dir>
The scratch --output is deliberate: state/test-runs/latest.json is polled by other
lanes as authoritative and a gate run must not overwrite it.
Of these 38 entries, 15 were also not passing in the previous complete run
(2026-08-11T02:57:53.443Z, 688 files) and 23 are NEW since it. That second number is the
whole argument for this file: 22 test files broke between two runs of the same tree
and nothing could tell you which, because both runs simply exited non-zero.
ARITHMETIC, RECONCILED 2026-08-12 -- read this before comparing the numbers above
with the array below, because they DO NOT match and the mismatch is not an error.
Everything above describes the SEED and is history: 38 entries = 35 fail + 1 timeout
+ 2 skip, and 699 + 35 + 1 + 2 = 737, which balances. The array is the CURRENT state
and holds 35 entries = 32 fail + 1 timeout + 2 skip. The difference is exactly the
three removals recorded in the wave-2 note below, each proven green before removal.
The seed paragraph is deliberately NOT rewritten to 35: it is the measurement that
created this file, and a baseline whose history is edited to agree with its present
cannot show anyone what changed. Only this note is added when the array moves.
The 2 skip entries are the two opt-in-gated Windows Task Scheduler mutation suites.
They are NOT failures and tools/test-ratchet.mjs no longer treats them as such (they
were making SHIP OK unreachable); they stay listed so that a skip appearing anywhere
ELSE is still read as a regression. Failing-file arithmetic for the ship gate is
therefore 32, not 35.
NEVER add an entry to make a red run go green without saying why in the note. The
note is the only thing standing between this file and a quarantine list.
LANE engine-red-tests (wave 2) lowered this baseline by 3, each PROVEN green on the
current tree immediately before removal (PowerShell, Node v22.19.0):
- tests/settings-surface-readonly.test.js -> now passes (exit 0, 4/4). Root cause: the
R1231 state-store repair made getStateStore() eagerly open+validate on first call, and
tool-registry.js + providers/web.js instantiated state-backed providers at MODULE LOAD,
so importing the registry opened the DB and crashed on the test's bare node:sqlite mock.
Fixed by deferring those instantiations to first use (registry lazy proxy; web lazy
default provider) -- import is now side-effect-free, eager-open preserved on first use.
- tests/measurement-honesty.js -> now passes (exit 0, 7 checks). Root cause: tools/
check-memory-board-unity.js:541 matched Win32_Process CommandLine without guarding the
empty read an unelevated cross-session query returns, silently dropping task-owned
servers. Fixed to surface empty CommandLine as undeterminable (never counted stale).
- tests/test-census.test.js -> now passes (exit 0). Self-fixed by the concurrent census
lane's re-pin to 197 (see the removed entry's own note); no engine-red-tests code change.
